noviscent_rules: AST004 (Unsandboxed Code Execution), AST005/AST008 (tool router/selection policy)
what_noviscent_can_detect_statically: eval()/exec()/subprocess execution inside a tool handler without sandboxing; tool dispatch without an allowlist.
test_scenario_used: DVMCP-05 Tool Shadowing (eval sink), DVAA-06 DNS Exfiltration via Tool Calls
measured_result: 0/2 detected. AST004 missed 2 direct eval() calls; DVAA-06's declarative JSON tool-config (shell:true, no domain allow-list) is outside the shape any current rule parses. AST005/AST008 misfired on unrelated safe code in the same file as DVMCP-05.
known_limitation_or_runtime_dependency: No rule currently inspects MCP tool-description/docstring content for embedded imperative instructions ("tool poisoning", DVMCP-02) -- a distinct, undetected MCP-specific pattern.

noviscent_rules: SP001 (Hardcoded Secret Detected, via gitleaks), TOOLS005 (Path Traversal in Tools), AST013 (Unrestricted Agent Delegation)
what_noviscent_can_detect_statically: Hardcoded API keys/tokens in source; unvalidated file-path parameters used in file reads; agent delegation to sub-agents without scope restriction.
test_scenario_used: DVAA-02 API Keys in Web-Served Files, DVMCP-07 Token Theft, DVMCP-03 Excessive Permission Scope, DVAA-08 Delegation Privilege Escalation
measured_result: 2/4 detected. SP001 caught both hardcoded-secret scenarios cleanly. TOOLS005 missed an unambiguous path-traversal pattern; AST013 missed a strong textual match to its own rule description.
known_limitation_or_runtime_dependency: SP001 detection depends on gitleaks (a separate scanner from the semgrep-based packs) being run alongside Engine A -- see benchmark-manifest.json's secondary_scanner disclosure.

noviscent_rules: SC002 (Unpinned Dependency), SC003 (Unverified Model Download), SC002b/SC003-bash variants
what_noviscent_can_detect_statically: Missing version pins in package.json/requirements.txt; unpinned pip/npm runtime installs; unverified wget of model-file extensions.
test_scenario_used: DVAA-04 Insecure Install (curl|sh), DVAA-05 Dependency Confusion, DVAA-07 MCP Capability Escalation, DVMCP-04 Rug Pull
measured_result: 0/4 on primary declared root cause. SC002 fired on DVAA-05 and DVAA-07's package.json files, but for an unrelated reason (caret version ranges) rather than the declared vulnerability (unclaimed-scope squatting / staged capability escalation).
known_limitation_or_runtime_dependency: Dependency-confusion risk requires cross-referencing external public-registry state, not visible from the file alone. Bash coverage for generic 'curl|sh' installers is narrower than 'wget of a model file' or 'pip/npm install' -- a real, fixable rule-coverage gap (see results-summary.md item 7).

noviscent_rules: TOOLS003 (Command Injection in Tool Handler), TOOLS006 (Unsafe Deserialization in Tool), AST004 (Unsandboxed Code Execution)
what_noviscent_can_detect_statically: Shell command construction from tool arguments; pickle/yaml/marshal deserialization of untrusted data; eval/exec/subprocess without sandboxing.
test_scenario_used: DVAA-01 Pickle Deserialization, DVAA-03 Command Injection (exec template), DVMCP-08 Malicious Code Execution, DVMCP-09 Remote Access Control
measured_result: 1/4 detected. TOOLS006 caught the pickle-deserialization scenario at the exact predicted line. TOOLS003 detected 0 of 6 command-injection sinks across DVAA-03/DVMCP-08/DVMCP-09 (2 languages).
known_limitation_or_runtime_dependency: TOOLS003's current pattern shape does not match f-string/template-literal command construction flowing into shell=True subprocess calls or Node exec() -- the single highest-value fix identified by this benchmark.

noviscent_rules: RAG001 (RAG Context in System Prompt) -- closest existing shape, not a full match
what_noviscent_can_detect_statically: Untrusted retrieved/ingested content flowing into a system prompt without boundary markers.

known_limitation_or_runtime_dependency: Generic tool-result construction from untrusted external content (not just system-prompt construction) is a gap; a heuristic rule (PRS001-H) produced 5 false positives elsewhere in the same file instead.
